title: Signal resilience matrix and rolling canary schedule for adaptive-rollouts
creator: Riley Patel
description:
Goal: Define an operationally-clear signal-to-action matrix and timing for our rolling canary process for new inference model variants and routing policies. This ticket scopes the acceptance gates, concrete thresholds, statistical checks, and an automated schedule that platform teams can reuse for A/B tests, canaries, and progressive rollouts across Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Background: Recent rollouts surfaced ambiguity in which metric breaches should trigger automatic rollback vs. human review. We need a compact, reproducible matrix mapping metric groups (latency, error surface, qualitative quality diagnostics, cost/unit) to actions (pause/reroute/rollback/escalate) and a staged traffic schedule with required sample sizes and observation windows.

Scope:
- Define metric groups and primary/secondary signals (latency p50/p95/p99, request_error_rate, model_quality_eval_score, top-k hallucination rate proxy, token-cost-per-request)
- Set concrete numeric thresholds and guardrail bands for automated gates and human-review gates
- Specify statistical test and confidence (e.g., sequential A/B with Bayes factor or t-test with min N) per signal
- Author a canonical rolling canary schedule (traffic ramp, wait windows, auto-binary decisions) for low/medium/high-risk launches
- Produce Grafana dashboard templates and recommended alerting rules (links below)
- Document operational playbook (who to page, runbook links, rollback steps) and handoff checklist for experiments

Out of scope: deep changes to routing engine, long-term eval infrastructure (handled in separate infra tickets).
acceptance_criteria: A single-table Signal Resilience Matrix exists mapping 6 metric groups to actions and owners
Numeric thresholds and SLO-based guardrails documented for low/medium/high risk profiles
Canonical rolling canary schedule with explicit traffic percentages, observation windows and minimum sample sizes
Grafana dashboard templates and alert rules linked and verified against staging telemetry
Runbook + escalation ladder checked into Confluence and referenced from the ticket
Cross-functional sign-off from Eng infra, Oncall, and Observability (Slack emoji approvals in comments)
